content.content:
worklog is the canonical tool for Preston's personal worklog system.

It reads and (eventually) writes a small markdown corpus at
$HOME/.local/share/worklog/ — a front-page WORK.md, a per-month archive, an
INDEX.md spine, and per-epic notes files. The tool replaces a set of bash
scripts that handled validation and skill deployment.

Usage:
  worklog [flags]
  worklog [command]

Available Commands:
  add         Add a new ticket, epic, or child of an epic (form by default for standalone tickets)
  adopt       Adopt a corpus that predates the store, or preview what that would do
  completion  Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  done        Archive a completed ticket (form by default; flag-driven for agents)
  edit        Set metadata fields on an existing ticket block
  feedback    List or append captured feedback
  freeze      Report, acquire, or release the code-enforced write freeze
  help        Help about any command
  hook        Emit Claude Code hook payloads (agent-invoked, not for humans)
  import      Import tickets from JSON (single object or array)
  install     Deploy skills, config, and devboard setup (the install.sh brain)
  link        Read, list, or update a ticket's named **Link**: entries
  migrate     Rehearse the worklog2 storage migration against a copy of live data
  note        Append a timestamped note to notes/<id>.md, or read existing notes
  pr          Read or update the **PR**: field on a ticket
  reindex     Rebuild INDEX.md from WORK.md + archive/ + notes/
  search      Search the worklog (INDEX-first, full-text fallback)
  serve       Serve the devboard dashboard (frontend + API, port 8484)
  standup     Daily standup report: completed yesterday, active today, blockers
  start       Promote a ticket to ## Now (cap-checked, start-dated)
  status      Print Now/Next/Someday in a styled, scriptable summary
  summarize   Status-report view of in-progress tickets, grouped by epic
  task        Update the devboard task file for in-flight work
  tui         Launch the interactive Bubble Tea view
  validate    Run all structural invariants over the worklog data dir
  verify      Report drift between live worklog/devboard data and the rewrite's rendered projections
  wait        Park a Now ticket into ## Waiting (cap-exempt holding area)

Flags:
      --dir string   worklog data directory (default $WORKLOG_DIR or ~/.local/share/worklog)
  -h, --help         help for worklog
  -v, --version      version for worklog

Use "worklog [command] --help" for more information about a command.

# CLI reference — JSON shapes, exit codes, error strings

Read this when you need a JSON field name, an exit code, or the exact error
a command emits. Flags and usage are not repeated here — run
`worklog <command> --help` for those.

- [Conventions](#conventions)
- [Exit codes](#exit-codes)
- [status](#status)
- [add](#add)
- [start](#start)
- [done](#done)
- [search](#search)
- [reindex](#reindex)
- [summarize](#summarize)
- [validate](#validate)

## Conventions

- `--json` mode: every command emits a single JSON document to stdout,
  success or error. Parse it as the single source of truth; ignore stderr
  unless it's a system-level error.
- Errors in `--json` mode are `{"error": "<message>"}`. Exit codes are
  identical between text and JSON modes.
- `worklog add` requires `--title` and `--id` when stdin is not a TTY,
  else it falls into the human form (which agents must not use).
- `worklog --dir <path>` overrides the data directory. Honors `WORKLOG_DIR`
  as fallback; when both are set, `--dir` wins.
- Cobra accepts `--dir` before or after the subcommand. Canonical form for
  readability: `worklog --dir <path> <subcommand> [--flags]`.
- `cap: 0` in `status --json` means **uncapped**, not zero-limit. Only
  `## Now` has a cap (5).

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | success, no violations |
| `1` | domain error (duplicate ID, invalid section, WORK.md missing) |
| `2` | `validate` found violations |

## Migrate command (internal/migrate, internal/cli/migrate.go)

`worklog migrate` (adb-worklog2-migrate) is the first thing to actually
run this design end to end. It stages a read-only copy of the live
worklog dir + devboard dir (never writes them — verified by a live-dir
checksum test), converts the copy via `convert.ReadCorpusDir` +
`convert.Load`, and reports whether entity identity held steady: an
id-set diff of every ticket and sub-item ULID between the pre- and
post-run state of a persisted SQLite db, plus stale rows the diff alone
can't see (`convert.Load` only upserts — nothing here deletes).

Mechanism, in order: stage (with size/mtime tear detection and one retry —
`ErrTornSnapshot`), copy-forward seed the working copy from the existing
output db (a plain read of `OUTPUT_PATH`; it is never opened for writing —
`convert.Load` runs against the working copy only), checkpoint
(`PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`) and close the working copy, then
atomically swap it into place — `OUTPUT_PATH` → `OUTPUT_PATH.bak` (one
generation, no rotation), working copy → `OUTPUT_PATH` — clearing any WAL
sidecar rather than carrying or orphaning it. All of it lives under one
directory: `--out`, `$WORKLOG_MIGRATION_DATA`, or
`~/.local/share/worklog-migration` by default.

Building this against the real mechanics (not just against `convert.Load`
in isolation) found and fixed two gaps in the identity guarantee the
design above describes: `carrySubItemIDs` didn't cover links, code refs,
needs-you or waiting-on (only plan steps, scorecard, decisions and note
entries), and feedback entries had no re-run identity at all, so
copy-forward would have duplicated every friction entry on every run. Both
are fixed in `internal/convert`; see the Identity section above.

Still not done here: skill text updates for the projection world
(`adb-skill-projection-update`); JSONL export (deferred, D9). The
production cutover itself — freeze, binary snapshot, retire old write
paths — shipped in `adb-cutover`; see "Adoption" below.

## Verify command (internal/verify, internal/cli/verify.go)

`worklog verify` (`adb-projection-render`) is the store/projection design's
first production caller: it stages a read-only snapshot of the live
worklog + devboard dirs (reusing `internal/migrate`'s `Stage`), converts it
into an in-memory store, renders that store's projections into a second
scratch dir via `RenderAll`, and reports field-level drift between the
staged snapshot and the render — surface by surface (WORK.md, notes,
archive, INDEX.md, FEEDBACK.md, devboard feed). It never writes to the
live worklog or devboard directories, under any outcome; the write-back
shipped separately, as `worklog adopt` (see "Adoption").

content.content:
## Customization points

If you want to change behavior, here's where to look. There's no config file —
behavior is defined in markdown that the agent reads.

Edit the repo copies under `skill/`, never the deployed ones — a
redeploy overwrites those. `worklog install --check` tells you when the two
have diverged.

| Want to change... | Edit this file | Look for |
|---|---|---|
| The cap of 5 | WORK.md policy block + [skill](skill/SKILL.md) "Hard rules" + [command](skill/claude/command.md) + this README's rules block | the literal number 5 |
| Section names (Now/Waiting/Next/Someday) | All of the above (rename consistently) | section headings |
| Ticket block format / required fields | [skill](skill/SKILL.md) "Ticket block format" | the markdown code fence |
| Archive entry format | [skill](skill/SKILL.md) "Archive entry format" | the markdown code fence |
| Auto-trigger aggressiveness | [skill](skill/SKILL.md) frontmatter `description:` (richer triggers = more eager auto-invoke) | YAML frontmatter |
| Where the data tree lives | Runtime: `--dir <path>` or `$WORKLOG_DIR` (flag wins). Permanently: the path is quoted in `skill/SKILL.md`, `skill/claude/command.md`, and this README — ripgrep for it. | `~/.local/share/worklog` |
| Add a new persistent section (e.g. `## Blocked`) | WORK.md seed + [skill](skill/SKILL.md) "Required behavior" | section list |

After editing the skill files in the repo, redeploy:

```bash
worklog install --check   # verify the deployed copies match the repo
worklog install           # deploy all four skills (dev-context, contract, fan-out, worklog)
../install.sh             # same, but obtains/updates the binary first
```

The repo's `skill/` dir is the single source of truth. `worklog install`
reads the install config (`~/.config/ai-devboard/targets`) and never writes
to a target you declined; with no config it detects the agent dirs present
under `$HOME`. It always deploys every skill, so a target you added by hand

content.text:
## Root cause

`WORKLOG_DIR` only relocates the markdown projection tree (WORK.md, INDEX.md, notes/, archive/, FEEDBACK.md — `model.NewWorkdir`, `internal/model/workdir.go:53`). It has no effect on two other data roots every write verb also touches:

- **The SQLite store** (source of truth). `openStoreForWrite` (`internal/cli/store_common.go:113`) resolves it via `storeDataDir()` (`internal/cli/task_store.go:174`), which reads `$WORKLOG_MIGRATION_DATA`, falling back to the fixed `~/.local/share/worklog-migration` — never `$WORKLOG_DIR`.
- **The devboard dir**, via `devboard.DataDir()` (`internal/devboard/devboard.go:221`), gated by its own `$DEVBOARD_DATA`.

So setting only `WORKLOG_DIR` splits the world in two: the store handle still points at the real, already-adopted, populated store, while the projection layout points at the new empty scratch directory. `openStoreForWrite` then calls `projection.EditedIn(s, layout)` (`internal/projection/projection.go:193`), which renders what the *real* store's tickets should look like as markdown and diffs that against files at the scratch path. Every file is absent there, and `EditedIn`'s "absent means it was deleted" rule (with only a narrow board-file-move exception) treats every one of them as a hand-edit. I reproduced this directly: pointing only `WORKLOG_DIR` at a fresh empty directory and running `worklog note` refused, listing ~70 files — the real corpus's `WORK.md`, `FEEDBACK.md`, `archive/2026-09.md`, and every epic's notes file — none of which the "colleague" ever touched.

This isn't a bug in the hand-edit guard itself (which is working as designed against a real, non-empty worklog dir); it's a documentation/API-surface gap. `worklog --help` and the README's "Where the data tree lives" row both state flatly that `--dir`/`$WORKLOG_DIR` is *the* data directory override, and `skill/references/cli.md` repeats that framing — none of them mention `$WORKLOG_MIGRATION_DATA` or `$DEVBOARD_DATA` as siblings that must move together for true isolation. The only place `$WORKLOG_MIGRATION_DATA` is documented at all is `docs/store-design.md`, framed as an internal detail of `worklog migrate`, not as "the other half of what you need to sandbox worklog."

## Recommendation

Two layers, since one is a quick doc fix and the other is the real fix:

1. **Unify the data roots.** Have the store and devboard paths derive from `WORKLOG_DIR`'s root by default (e.g. `<root>/store/worklog.db`, `<root>/devboard`) instead of each independently defaulting to a fixed `~/.local/share/...` path. Keep `$WORKLOG_MIGRATION_DATA`/`$DEVBOARD_DATA` as explicit overrides for people who want to mix-and-match, but make "one env var / one flag = fully isolated instance" true by default — that's what the docs already promise.
2. **Until that lands, fix the docs/help text** (`--help` in `internal/cli/root.go`, README's "Where the data tree lives" row, `skill/references/cli.md`) to say explicitly that full isolation requires setting `WORKLOG_DIR`, `WORKLOG_MIGRATION_DATA`, and (if devboard is enabled) `DEVBOARD_DATA` together — not `WORKLOG_DIR` alone.

A secondary, independent hardening: `EditedIn`'s absent-file branch can't currently distinguish "a human deleted this projection" from "this store has never been rendered into this directory at all." Detecting the latter (e.g., no projection files exist yet anywhere under the target root) and rendering fresh instead of refusing would make the specific "brand-new empty scratch dir" case safe even without root-unification, though it wouldn't fix the underlying multi-root confusion on its own.
